Electronic meters 
2456. SHRI VEDPRAKASH P. GOYAL: Will the Minister of POWER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the new electronic meter installed by power 
companies are manipulated by companies in their favour; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether any comparative study has been done regarding increase in 
power bills after installation of electronic meter; and 
(d) if so, what are findings, give details? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P.M. SAYEED): (a) to (d) Section 55 
of the Electricity Act, 2003 provides that no licensee shall supply electricity 
exept through installation of a correct meter in accordance with the regulations 
made in this behalf by the Central Electricity Authority (CEA). Further, State 
Electricity Regulatory Commissions are required to specify an Electricity 
Supply Code under section 50 of the Act. Contravention of regulations is a 
punishable offence as per the provisions of the Act. 
Electronic meters read all the el ectricity consumption including the 
electricity consumed by a zero watt bulb (6 to 12 watts). These meters record 
the consumption of the electronic gadgets even when they are in stand by mode 
while the mechanical meters are unable to record this consumption because of 
their higher tolerance limit. Mechanical meters tend to get slower with the 
passage of time because of wear and tear in the measuring components. 
The Delhi Electricity Regulatory Commission has informed that there have 
been consumers' complaints regarding inaccurate readings after installation of 
Electronic meters. The DERC and also  the Distribution Companies have 
separately conducted meter-testing drives. The latest drive conducted by the 
Distribution Companies was in associ ation with Central Power Research 
Institute (CPRI), an autonomous body of the Ministry of Power, Government 
of India. The results from this drive show that 515 meters have been tested in 
the presence of CPRI in the areas of BSES Yamuna Power Ltd. and BSES 
Rajdhani Power Ltd. (till mid June 2005) and all meters were found to be 
within limits. As regards the area of North Delhi Power Ltd., 45 meters have 
been tested till the end of 
157 

RAJYA SABHA [17 August, 2005] 
July 2005 and all meters were found to be within limits excepting one which 
was found to be slow.

Effect of reduced discharge of water flow on power generation 
2470. DR. K. KASTURIRANGAN: Will the Minister of POWER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that there is reduced discharge across Sutlej, Beas 
and Yamuna Basins, that is resulting in reduced power generation in the recent 
years; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether Government has any plans to augment the water flow to enable 
power houses to operate their optimal capacity; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P.M. SAYEED): (a) The inflows in 
Sutlej during the years 2000-01, 2001-02, 2004-05 and in Beas during the year 
2002-03, 2003-04 and 2004-05 have been less and below dependable year 
inflows. The available flow data for river Yamuna does not clearly indicate 
natural reduction in the flow of river Yamuna. During the year 2004-05 
discharge in Yamuna basin was on a lower side than the discharge available in 
the previous year. The reduction in inflows has resulted in reduced power 
generation. However, inflows in Sutlej and Beas during the current year 
2005-06 so far have been very good. Consequently the generation has also 
been higher than the previous year. 
(b) Inflows in the rivers are contributed by snow melt and rains. The 
reduced inflows in the above mentioned years has been due to less rains/ snow 
fall in the catchment area. 
(c) and (d) Hydro Electric St ations are either of run-of-river type or 
storage type. Generation in run-of-river power stations depends upon the 
discharge available in the river and there is either no pondage or very less 
pondage available. As such, generation in such plants would depend mainly on 
the inflows which in turn depends upon rainfall/snowfall in the catchment area 
of these stations. Reservoir based stations enable water to be stored in the 
monsoon period which could be utilised during lean period of the year. 
Government is having plans to construct both types of stations depending upon 
water availability and topography of the site. 
171 

RAJYA SABHA [17 August, 2005] 
In Sutlej basin, Bhakra (1325 MW) is a reservoir based station in operation 
and Khab Storage scheme (636 MW) is under investigation. In Beas basin, Pong 
(396 MW) is a reservoir based station in operation. In Yamuna Basin, Lakhwar-
vyasi (420 MW), Kishau (600 MW) and Renuka (40 MW) are the planned 
reservoir based projects. The water flow from reservoir schemes can be 
regulated to enable power houses to operate to their optimal capacity.

Statement  
Salient features of the National Electricity Policy 
1. Aims at accelerated development of power sector, providing supply 
of electricity to all areas and pr otecting interests of consumers and 
other stakeholders. 
2. Objectives: 
♦ Access to Electricity -Available for all households in next five years. 
♦ Availability of Power - Demand to be fully met by 2012. Energy and peaking 
shortages to be overcome and spinning reserve to be available. 
♦ Supply of Reliable and Quality Power of specified standards in an efficient 
manner and at reasonable rates. 
♦ Per capita availability of electricity to be increased to over 1000 units by 
2012. 
♦ Minimum lifeline consumption of 1 unit/household/day as merit good by year 
2012. 
179 

RAJYA SABHA [17 August, 2005] 
♦ Financial Turnaround and Commercial Viability of Electricity Sector. 
♦ Protection of consumers' interests. 
 
3. CEA to notify first National Electricity Plan in six months with a 
perspective up 12th Plan period. The Plan prepared by CEA to be used by 
prospective generating companies, transmission utilities and 
transmission/distribution licensees as reference document. 
4. Development of Rural Electrification Distribution backbone, village 
electrification and household electrification to achieve the NCMP target 
of completing household electrification in next five years. Financial 
support in terms of capital subsidy to States for rural electrification. 
Special preference to Dalit Bastis, Tribal Areas and other weaker 
sections for rural electrification. REC to be nodal agency for rural 
electrification at Central Government level. 
5. Creation of adequate generation capacity with a spinning reserve of at 
least 5% by 2012 with availability of installed capacity at 85%. 
6. Full development of hydro potential. Provision of long tenor finance for 
these projects. 
7. Choice of fuel for thermal generation to be based on economics of 
generation and supply of electricity. 
8. Development of National Grid. 
9. Cost of recovery of service from consumers at tariff reflecting efficient 
costs to ensure financial viability of the sector. 
10. Provision of support to lifeline consumers (households below poverty line 
having consumption of 30 units per month) in terms of tariffs. 
11. Availability Based Tariff (ABT) to be extended to State level for better grid 
discipline through economic signaling.. 
12. Special emphasis on time bound reduction of transmission and 
distribution losses. 
13. Measures to promote competition aimed at consumer benefits. 
14. Reliability and quality of power supply to be monitored by State 
Electricity Regulatory Commissions. 
180 

[17 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
15. Exploitation of non-conventional evergy sources such as small 
hydro, solar, biomass and wind for additional power generation 
capacity. 
Other Features 
16. Emphasis on achieving higher efficiency levels of generating plants 
through necessary renovation and modernization. 
17. Central Government to facilitate the continued development of national 
grid. CTU and STU to undertake coordinated planning and development. 
18. Transmission capacity to have redundancy level and margins as per 
international standards. 
19. Adequate transitional financial s upport for reforming power utilities. 
Encouragement for private sector participation in distribution. 
20. The State Regulatory Commissions to put in place independent third 
party meter testing arrangement. 
21. Support for adoption of IT system for ensuring correct billing to 
consumers. 
22. Speedy implementation of stringent measures against theft of 
electricity. 
23. Full emphasis on augmentation of R&D base. Mission approach for 
identified priorities areas. 
24. Demand side management through energy conservation measures. Labels 
regarding energy efficiency to be displayed on appliances. Efficient 
agricultural pumpsets and efficient lighting technologies to be promoted. 
Appropriate tariff structure for managing the peak load. 
25. Special attention for developing training infrastructure in the field of 
regulation, trading and power market. 
26.. For giving boost to renewable and non-conventional energy sources, a 
prescribed percentage of power, as specified by State Regulatory 
Commissions, to be purchased from such sources of energy at the earliest. 
27. Necessary regulations and appointing Ombudsman for redressal of

Statement  
Information regarding faulty digital meters 
Orissa Electricity Regulatory Commission 
A specific case has been registered by the consumers against CESCO in case No. 
7/2003 dated 11.9.2003 and the Commission after thorough scrutiny and hearing both 
the parties directed as under:— 
"In the persent scenario aggressive metering is highly required to check the rising trend 
of distribution losses. So, any effort by any Distribution Licensee for a mega-metering 
project is most welcome. There is no doubt that CESCO's effort to replace the 
existing defective meters with better quality meter is appreciable. The Commission 
was also given to understand by CESCO that around 80,000 meters have been 
installed so far in various areas under CESCO and not a single complaint from a 
genuine consumer has been received relating to the newly installed meter. The report of the 
Chief Elelctrical Inspector revealed that all these meters confirm to the permissible 
limits as stipulated in IS-13010-1990. The special features of the electromechanical 
meter are polycarbonate case and magnetic suspension bearing with high level of 
accuracy under various conditions of load. The transparent case makes it easy for 
detection of any tampering. 
In the above circumstances, the Commission considers that the general apprehension of 
the consumers/general public about the accurate reading of these Chinese meters is 
untenable. However, in case of any individual compliant, the respondent licensee should 
act promptly to do the needful." 
Punjab State Electricity Regulatory Commission 
There is a general feeling amongst the consumers that the digital meters are 
faster and unreliable. The Board, on the other hand, feels that the digital meters are 
accurate and not so easily tampered whereas mechanical meters tend to get slower 
with the passage of time and are easily tampered and as such the digital meters are 
resisted by the consumers. However, no detailed and reliable studies have been 
conducted by the Board in this regard and as such it is not possible to say that the 
digital meters are actually faulty or unreliable. 
191 

RAJYA SABHA [17 August, 2005] 
Jharkhand State Electricity Regulatory Commission 
The Commission has not received any complaints regarding faulty and 
unreliability of the digital meters till date. 
Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission 
No such complaint regarding the digital meters being found to be faulty and unreliable 
has been received in the Commission. 
Assam Electricity Regulatory Commission 
No specific complaints have been received on new meters installed in consumer 
premises. 
Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission 
Report of the joint inspection by Government Electrical Inspector, Consumer 
representatives and Licensee do not reveal that the digital meters are unreliable. 
Himachal Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission 
The percentage of faulty meters reported by Himachal Pradesh State Electricity Board 
(HPSEB) is about 2%. As such it cannot be construed that electronic energy meters are 
faulty and unreliable. 
Government of NCT of Delhi 
In view of complaints being received form the various quarters, the Delhi Electricity 
Regulatory Commission (DERC) had set up a committee in August 2003 to look into 
various complaints being received in the Commission regarding faulty meters. The 
Committee also had officials from a prominent NGO namely Common Cause. The 
Committee undertook testing of almost 375 meters randomly selected from the stores of 
Distribution Companies at the test bench set up in the Commission. The Committee had 
observed that 91 % of meters recorded consumption limits within prescribed levels given in 
the Indian Electricity Rules; 2% of meters were found to be slow and 0.5% were found 
faster than the prescribed limit. About 5% of meters, however, were found to be defective 
seemingly due to design features. Subsequently, Distribution Companies had carried out a 
meter testing drive from 16.7.2004 to 18.8.2004 and , found only about 0.7% meters to 
be faster than the specified limits.

† 2493. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI: Will the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware of the fact that irregularities are being 
committed on a large scale in 'Food for Work' scheme being run by Government in 
Madhya Pradesh; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the details of unemployed persons having been provided with employment in 
Madhya Pradesh under 'Food for Work' scheme as on date? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI A. NARENDRA): (a) and (b) There are no reports of large scale 
irregularities in the implementation of National Food for Work Programme in Madhya 
Pradesh. Since, the programme has been launched almost seven months ago, there

implementing/ executing agencies. Gradually the implementing agencies are picking

up and pace of utilization of resources has also increased. However, any report of 
irregularity is taken seriously and the facts of the case are immediately

provide additional supplementary wage employment in the rural areas of the 
identified 150 most backward Districts and as such the Physical output is

Incentives to growers of bio-diesel plants 
2497. SHRIMATI MOHSINA KIDWAI: Will the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government's attention has been drawn to the news item under the 
caption"Power Ministry Malls Sugarcane approach" for bio-diesel which appeared 
in Media; 
(b) if so, what incentive Government propose to offer to the growers of bio-diesel plants and 
by when such incentives are likely to be announced; and 
(c) if the answer to part(b) above is in negative, what are reasons thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (A. NARENDRA): (a) to (c) The news item referred to in the 
question appeared in The Statesman dated 5th September, 2004. This approach advocates 
growing of bio-diesel plants in advance before the required processing facilities are set up. 
For promotion of bio-diesel production, Jatropha curcas has been identified as a 
suitable plant for extensive cultivation. However, since this plant is a new introduction 
in the country and has no history of cultivation as a mono-crop and relevant data base on 
varieties, aronomic practices, productivity etc. is presently lacking, the Ministry of Rural 
Development has submitted a Detailed project Report (DPR) for approval of the 
Planning Commission to launch a demonstration project, under which Jatropha cultivation 
would be taken up on 4 lakh hectares in various States, primarily on degraded forest 
lands and Panchayat/community wastelands. If this demonstration project proves 
successful, Jatropha plantation would be taken up on a large 
208

scale on private lands also at a later date. The desirability of providing suitable 
incentives to private growers of Jatropha would be considered at that time.

2501. SHRILALIT SURI: Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased to state: 
(a) the specific reasons for the poor performance particularly in the field-of exports 
of Central Cottage Industries Corporation of India Ltd. New Delhi during the years 
2001-02 and 2003-04; 
(b) the steps proposed to be taken to improve the working of the corporation; 
and 
(c) whether any higher targets of production and exports have been fixed for the 
years 2005-06 and 2006-07, if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI SHANKERSINH VAGHELA): (a) The 
Central Cottage Industries Corporation of India Ltd. (CCIC), New Delhi is mainly engaged 
in the retail marketing of handioom and handicraft items within the country. The foreign 
exchange earning of CCIC though sales to foreign tourists against foreign currencies was 
Rs. 3.99 crore in 2001-02 and Rs. 3.38 crore in 2003-04; 
(b) The following steps have been taken to improve the working of the 
corporation: 
(i) strengthening the operations of emporia, 
(ii) improvementin merchandise, 
(iii) cost control, 
(iv) setting up of showrooms on franchise basis, and 
(v) booking of bulk/institutional orders. 
(c) The CCIC is not involved in production of handicrafts/ handlooms. 
It is a retail trading organization and purchases handicrafts/ handlooms 
goods from artisans/ craftsmen. For 2005-06 turnover target of 
Rs. 68.50 crores has been fixed, which is an increase of 11% (approx)

Government has sanctioned five Hi-Tech Weaving Parks at Tamil Nadu, Karnataka 
and Andhra Pradesh. The executing Agencies of two Parks at Palladam and Hyderabad
